paragraphs: Shore Bancshares, Inc. was incorporated under the laws of Maryland on March 15, 1996 and is the bank holding company for Shore United Bank, N.A,. Throughout this report, references to the "Company," "we," "our," and "us," and similar terms refer to the consolidated entity consisting of Shore Bancshares, Inc. and its subsidiaries. "Shore Bancshares" refers solely to the parent holding company, and the "Bank" refers solely to Shore Bancshares' subsidiary bank, Shore United Bank, N.A.

Shore Bancshares is registered as a financial holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the "BHC Act"). The Company is the largest independent financial holding company headquartered on the Eastern Shore of Maryland. The Company conducts business primarily through the Bank. The Bank provides consumer and commercial banking products and services and secondary mortgage lending, trust, wealth management and financial planning services. The Company offered title services through its wholly-owned subsidiary, Mid-Maryland Title Company, Inc. (the "Title Company"), which engaged in residential and commercial real estate settlement activities and offered title insurance policies, title search and lien satisfaction services. The Title Company ceased conducting real estate closings effective March 31, 2025. The Company and the Bank are Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employers.

The Bank, which traces its origin to 1876, is a national banking association chartered under the laws of the United States. The Bank currently operates 40 full-service branches and 10 loan production and administration offices, and provides a full range of commercial and consumer banking products and services to individuals, businesses, and other organizations in Maryland, Delaware and Virginia. The Bank's deposits are insured up to applicable legal limits by the FDIC.

Services provided to businesses include commercial checking, savings, certificates of deposit and overnight investment sweep accounts. The Bank offers all forms of commercial lending, including secured and unsecured loans, working capital loans, lines of credit, term loans, accounts receivable financing, real estate acquisition and development loans, construction loans and letters of credit. Treasury management services are also available, such as merchant card processing services, remote deposit capture, ACH origination, digital banking and telephone banking services.

Services provided to individuals include checking accounts, various savings programs, mortgage loans, home improvement loans, installment and other personal loans, credit cards, personal lines of credit, automobile and other consumer financing, trust administration, wealth management, safe deposit boxes, debit cards, 24-hour telephone banking, internet banking, mobile banking and 24-hour ATM services. Additionally, the Bank has Saturday hours and extended hours on certain evenings during the week for added customer convenience.

The Company's business strategy is to establish a leading community banking franchise that delivers exceptional financial services to the communities we serve. This strategy has been implemented over the past several years through a combination of organic and strategic growth, both within and contiguous to our existing footprint.

On July 1, 2023, the Company completed the acquisition of The Community Financial Corporation ("TCFC") and its wholly-owned subsidiary Community Bank of the Chesapeake ("CBTC"). The transaction expanded the Bank's footprint into the Southern Maryland Counties of Charles, St. Mary's and Calvert and the greater Fredericksburg area in Virginia, which includes Fredericksburg City as well as Stafford and Spotsylvania Counties. At the time of the acquisition, TCFC had $2.4 billion in assets, $454.5 million in investments, $1.8 billion in loans, $2.1 billion in deposits, $150.6 million in brokered deposits, $69.0 million in Federal Home Loan Bank (the "FHLB") advances and $32.0 million in subordinated debt and trust preferred debentures. The excess of the fair value of net TCFC assets acquired over the merger consideration resulted in an $8.8 million bargain purchase gain.
The Bank originates loans including commercial real estate, residential real estate, construction, commercial and consumer.

•Commercial Real Estate ("CRE") and Other Non-Residential Real Estate Loans. The Bank's CRE loans are primarily secured by commercial buildings, multi-family buildings, agricultural purpose consumer properties, service industry buildings such as restaurants and hotels, retail buildings and general purpose business space. The Bank attempts to mitigate the risks associated with these loans through financial analyses, conservative underwriting procedures, including loan-to-value ratio standards, obtaining additional collateral and management's knowledge of the local economy in which the Bank lends.

•Residential Real Estate Loans. The Bank originates residential mortgage loans that are to be held in our loan portfolio as well as loans that are intended for sale in the secondary market. Loans sold in the secondary market are primarily sold to investors with which the Bank maintains a correspondent relationship. These loans are made in conformity with standard government-sponsored enterprise underwriting criteria required by the investors to assure maximum eligibility for resale in the secondary market and are approved either by the Bank's underwriter or the correspondent's underwriter. Additionally, loans that are sold into the secondary market are typically residential long-term loans (15 or more years), generally with fixed rates of interest. Loans retained for the Bank's portfolio typically include loans that periodically reprice or mature prior to the end of an amortized term. Generally, loans are sold with mortgage servicing rights retained, which includes loans sold to the Federal National Mortgage Association ("Fannie Mae") or the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation ("Freddie Mac"). As of December 31, 2025, the Bank was servicing $343.8 million in loans for Fannie Mae and $105.6 million in loans for Freddie Mac.

•Construction Loans. The Bank provides commercial and residential real estate construction loans to builders and individuals. Residential construction loans are usually granted based upon "as completed" appraisals and are secured by the property under construction. Additional collateral may be taken if loan-to-value ratios exceed 80%. Site inspections are performed to determine pre-specified stages of completion before loan proceeds are disbursed. These loans typically have maturities of six to twelve months and may have fixed or variable rate features. Permanent financing options for individuals include fixed and variable rate loans with three- and five-year balloon features and one-, three- and five-year adjustable rate mortgage loans. The Bank attempts to mitigate risks associated with these loans through conservative underwriting procedures such as loan-to-value ratios of 80% or less at origination, obtaining additional collateral when prudent, and closely monitoring construction projects to control disbursement of funds on loans.

•Commercial Loans. The Bank originates secured and unsecured loans for business purposes. Commercial loans are typically secured by real estate, accounts receivable, inventory, equipment and/or other assets of the business. Repayment is often dependent upon the successful operation of the business and may be affected by adverse conditions in the local economy or real estate market. The financial condition and cash flow of commercial borrowers is therefore carefully analyzed during the loan approval process, and continues to be monitored by obtaining business financial statements, personal financial statements and income tax returns. The frequency of this ongoing analysis depends upon the size and complexity of the credit and collateral that secures the loan. It is also the Bank's general policy to obtain personal guarantees from the principals of the commercial loan borrowers.

•Consumer Loans. A variety of consumer loans are offered to customers, including home equity loans, marine loans and other secured and unsecured lines of credit and term loans. Certain consumer loans are originated by a third-party on behalf of the Company. Careful analysis of an applicant's creditworthiness is performed before granting credit, and ongoing monitoring of loans outstanding is performed in an effort to minimize risk of loss by identifying problem loans early. The Company discontinued the issuance of new marine loans in June 2023 and only services the existing portfolio as of December 31, 2025.

•Credit Card Loans. The Bank offered unsecured credit card loans to commercial and consumer customers. Credit risk factors include the borrower's continuing financial stability, which can be adversely impacted by job loss, divorce, illness or personal bankruptcy, among other factors. The Company discontinued the issuance of new credit cards in April 2024 (except to select existing credit card customers) and only services the existing portfolio as of December 31, 2025.

headings: Risks Related to the Economy, Financial Markets, Interest Rates and Liquidity
The geographic concentration of our operations makes us susceptible to downturns in local economic conditions.
Changes in interest rates may adversely affect our earnings and financial condition.
Inflation can have an adverse impact on our business and on our customers.
Insufficient liquidity could impair our ability to fund operations and jeopardize our financial condition, growth and prospects.
Our business may be adversely affected by unfavorable economic, market, and political conditions.
Our investment securities portfolio is subject to credit risk, market risk, and liquidity risk.

Our allowance for credit losses may not be adequate to cover our actual credit losses; additions to the allowance for credit losses could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
We may not be able to adequately measure and limit our credit risk, which could lead to unexpected losses.
Our commercial real estate lending activities expose us to increased lending risks and related loan losses.
Imposition of limits by the bank regulators on commercial real estate lending activities could curtail our growth and adversely affect our earnings.
Our concentration of residential mortgage loans exposes us to increased lending risks.
An increase in nonperforming assets would adversely impact earnings.
Appraisals may not accurately describe the value of our collateral.
Our future success will depend on our ability to compete effectively in the highly competitive financial services industry.
The loss of key personnel could disrupt our business.
Our funding sources may prove insufficient to replace deposits and support our future growth.
Income from mortgage-banking operations is volatile and we may incur losses with respect to our mortgage-banking operations that could negatively affect our earnings.
Any delays in our ability to foreclose on delinquent mortgage loans may increase our costs and expose us to greater losses.

The strict enforcement of federal laws regarding cannabis could result in our inability to continue to provide banking services to marijuana-related businesses and expose us to legal action by the federal government.
Our risk management framework may not be effective in mitigating risks and/or losses to us.
Risks Related to our Financial Statements
We may incur impairment charges on our investment securities, which could adversely impact our results of operations, liquidity, financial condition, or growth prospects.
Impairment goodwill, other intangible assets, or deferred tax assets could require charges to earnings, which would adversely impact on our results of operations.
Changes in accounting standards or interpretation of new or existing standards may affect how we report our financial condition and results of operations.

The Current Expected Credit Loss ("CECL") accounting standard could require us to increase our allowance for credit losses and may have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
Our accounting estimates and risk management processes rely on analytical and forecasting models.
We have previously identified material weaknesses in our internal controls.
We depend on the accuracy and completeness of information about customers and counterparties and our financial condition could be adversely affected if we rely on inaccurate information.
Operational risks, including system failures, human error, and third-party dependencies could adversely affect our business.
Risks Related to Cybersecurity and Technology
Our information systems may experience an interruption or breach in security.
Security breaches and other disruptions could compromise our information and expose us to liability, which would cause our business and reputation to suffer.
Failure to comply with privacy and information security laws could expose us to liability.
Our reliance on third party vendors could expose us to additional cyber risk and liability.
We outsource certain aspects of our data processing to certain third-party providers, which may expose us to additional risk.
We are at risk of increased losses from fraud.
Failure to keep up with technological change in the financial services industry could have a material adverse effect on our competitive position or profitability.
Risks Relating to the Regulation of our Industry
We operate in a highly regulated environment, which could restrain our growth and profitability.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves risks, including the possibility that the value of the investment could fall substantially and that dividends or other distributions could be reduced or eliminated. Investors should carefully consider the following risk factors before making an investment decision regarding our stock. The following risk factors may cause our future earnings to be lower or our financial condition to be less favorable than expected, which could adversely affect the value of, and return on, an investment in the Company. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may cause earnings to be lower or may adversely impact our financial condition. Investors should also consider the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, as well as in the documents incorporated by reference into this Form 10-K, as the same may be updated from time to time by our future filings with the SEC under the Exchange Act.

Our banking operations are concentrated in eastern and southern Maryland, Delaware and northern Virginia. Our success depends in part upon economic conditions in these markets. The Washington, D.C. metropolitan area is characterized by a significant number of businesses that are federal government contractors or subcontractors, or that depend on such businesses for a significant portion of their revenues. In addition, federal government employees make up a significant proportion of the population of the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. Reductions in the federal workforce through layoffs and buyouts, furloughs of government employees or government contractors, as well as cancelling government contracts and other impacts from declining government spending, lapses in appropriations, or changes in fiscal appropriations could have adverse impacts on other businesses in our market and the general economy of the greater Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. Adverse changes in economic conditions in our markets could limit growth in loans and deposits, impair our ability to collect amounts due on loans, increase problem loans and charge-offs and otherwise negatively affect our performance and financial condition. Declines in real estate values could cause some of our residential and commercial real estate loans to be inadequately collateralized, which would expose us to a greater risk of loss if the recovery on amounts due on defaulted loans is resolved by selling the real estate collateral under duress or to expedite payment.

Our net income depends to a great extent upon the level of net interest income, which is the difference between the interest income earned on loans, investments, and other interest-earning assets, and the interest paid on interest-bearing liabilities, such as deposits and borrowings. Net interest income is affected by changes in market interest rates because different types of assets and liabilities may react differently, and at different times, to market interest rate changes. When interest-bearing liabilities mature or re-price more quickly than interest-earning assets in a period, an increase in market rates of interest could reduce net interest income. Similarly, when interest-earning assets mature or re-price more quickly than interest-bearing liabilities, falling interest rates could reduce net interest income.

Changes in market interest rates are affected by many factors beyond our control, including inflation, unemployment, money supply, fiscal policies of the U.S. government, domestic and international events, and events in U.S. and other financial markets. We attempt to manage our risk from changes in market interest rates by adjusting the rates, maturity, re-pricing, and balances of the different types of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, but interest rate risk management techniques are not exact. As a result, a rapid increase or decrease in interest rates could have an adverse effect on our results of operations. Changes in the market interest rates for types of products and services in various markets also may vary significantly from location to location and over time based upon competition and local or regional economic factors.

For further discussion regarding the impact of interest rate movements on net interest income, see Item 7A of this report. The results of any interest rate sensitivity simulation model depend upon a number of assumptions regarding customer behavior, movement of interest rates and cash flows, any of which may prove to be inaccurate.

Inflation generally increases the cost of goods and services we use in our business operations, as well as labor costs. We may find that we need to give higher than normal raises to employees and start new employees at a higher wage. Furthermore, our clients are also affected by elevated inflation and the rising costs of goods and services used in their households and businesses, which could have a negative impact on their ability to repay their loans with us. Historically, the Federal Reserve has increased the federal funds target rate in an effort to combat elevated inflation. Market interest rates generally increase in response to the Federal Reserve's actions. Higher market interest rates increase borrowing costs and depress loan demand. As market interest rates rise, the value of our investment securities generally decreases, although this effect can be less pronounced for floating rate instruments. Higher interest rates increase the attractiveness of alternative investment and savings products, like U.S. Treasury securities and money market funds, which can make it difficult to attract and retain deposits. Sustained higher interest could weaken economic activity. A deterioration in economic conditions in the United States and our markets could result in a further increase in loan delinquencies and nonperforming assets, decreases in loan collateral values, and a decrease in demand for our products and services, all of which, in turn, would adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

paragraphs: The Company reported net income for the year ended December 31, 2025 of $59.5 million, or $1.78 diluted earnings per common share, compared to $43.9 million, or $1.32 diluted earnings per common share, for the year ended December 31, 2024. The Company's return on average assets, return on average common equity and return on average tangible common equity were 0.98%, 10.52% and 14.09%, respectively, for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to 0.74%, 8.35% and 12.21%, respectively, for the year ended December 31, 2024. For additional details, see "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures." The increase in net income in 2025 compared to 2024 was primarily due to higher net interest income ("NII") driven by loan growth in 2025 coupled with loans and deposits repricing favorably. These were partially offset by a higher provision for credit losses of $3.6 million.

paragraphs: Shore Bancshares, Inc. 於1996年3月15日根據馬裏蘭州法律設立，為Shore United Bank, N.A. 的銀行控股公司。本報告中，提及 "本公司"、"我們"、"我們的" 及 "我們" 等類似詞彙，均指由Shore Bancshares, Inc. 及其子公司組成的合併實體。"Shore Bancshares" 係指 solely 父公司，而 "Bank" 則係指Shore Bancshares 的子公司銀行Shore United Bank, N.A.

Shore Bancshares 已根據1956年銀行控股公司法案（"BHC Act"）經註冊為金融控股公司。本公司為位於馬裏蘭州東岸的規模最大的獨立金融控股公司。本公司業務主要透過銀行進行。銀行提供消費者及商業銀行產品與服務，並提供次級房貸貸款、信託、財富管理及財務規劃服務。本公司曾透過其全資子公司Mid-Maryland Title Company, Inc.（"Title Company"）提供地產過戶服務，該子公司從事住宅及商業不動產過戶活動，並提供地產保險、地產查詢及貸款清償服務。Title Company 於2025年3月31日起停止進行不動產過戶業務。本公司及銀行為肯定行動/平等機會僱主。
銀行可追溯至1876年，為根據美國法律設立的國家銀行協會。銀行目前擁有40家全功能分行及10家貸款業務與行政辦公室，並為馬裏蘭州、德拉瓦州及維吉尼亞州的個人、企業及其他組織提供完整的商業及消費者銀行產品與服務。銀行的存款由FDIC根據適用法律限額投保。
對企業提供的服務包括商業支票帳戶、儲蓄帳戶、存款憑證及過夜投資掃描帳戶。銀行提供所有形式的商業貸款，包括擔保及無擔保貸款、營運資金貸款、信貸線、定期貸款、應收帳款融資、不動產購置及開發貸款、建設貸款及信用證。此外，還提供財務管理服務，例如商家卡處理服務、遠端存款掃描、ACH發起、數位銀行及電話銀行服務。
對個人提供的服務包括支票帳戶、各種儲蓄方案、房貸貸款、房屋改善貸款、 installment 及其他個人貸款、信用卡、個人信貸線、汽車及其他消費者融資、信託管理、財富管理、保險箱、提款卡、24小時電話銀行、網際網路銀行、行動銀行及24小時ATM服務。此外，銀行提供週六營業時間及週間特定晚上延長營業時間，以增加客戶便利性。
本公司的業務策略為建立領導地位的社區銀行品牌，為所服務的社區提供卓越的金融服務。此策略已透過過去數年內的有機及戰略性成長，實現在現有業務範圍內及周邊地區。

2023年7月1日，本公司完成收購The Community Financial Corporation（"TCFC"）及其全資子公司Community Bank of the Chesapeake（"CBTC"）。此交易將銀行的業務範圍擴展至馬裏蘭州的Charles、St. Mary's及Calvert縣，以及維吉尼亞州的Fredericksburg地區，包括Fredericksburg市及Stafford和Spotsylvania縣。在收購時，TCFC擁有2.4十億美元資產、454.5百萬美元投資、1.8十億美元貸款、2.1十億美元存款、150.6百萬美元經紀存款、69.0百萬美元Federal Home Loan Bank（"FHLB"）貸款及32.0百萬美元次級債務及信託優先債券。所取得TCFC淨資產公允價值超過合併對價的部分，產生8.8百萬美元的 bargain purchase gain。
銀行發放貸款包括商業不動產、住宅不動產、建設、商業及消費者貸款。
•不動產貸款（"不動產貸款"）及其他非住宅不動產貸款。本銀行的不動產貸款主要以商業大樓、多單位住宅大樓、農業用途消費性不動產、服務業大樓如餐廳與旅館、零售大樓及一般用途商業空間為擔保。本銀行透過財務分析、保守的貸款審核程序，包括貸款價值比標準、取得額外擔保品及管理層對貸款地區總體經濟的瞭解，以降低這些貸款的風險。

•住宅不動產貸款。本銀行發放住宅抵押貸款，這些貸款將存於我們的貸款組閤中，或有意出售至次級市場。出售至次級市場的貸款主要出售給與本銀行有對應關係的投資者。這些貸款依照投資者要求的標準政府 sponsored 企業貸款審核准則發放，以確保在次級市場的最高可售性，並由本銀行貸款審核員或對應機構的貸款審核員批准。此外，出售至次級市場的貸款通常為住宅長期貸款（15 年或更長），通常為固定利率。本銀行保留的貸款通常包括定期重價或在償還期結束前到期的貸款。通常，貸款出售時會保留房貸服務權，包括出售至美國聯邦住宅貸款銀行（"Fannie Mae"）或美國聯邦住宅抵押貸款公司（"Freddie Mac"）的貸款。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本銀行為 Fannie Mae 服務 343.8 百萬美元的貸款，為 Freddie Mac 服務 105.6 百萬美元的貸款。

•建設貸款。本銀行為建築師及個人提供商業及住宅不動產建設貸款。住宅建設貸款通常根據 "完工後" 的評估發放，並以正在建設的財產為擔保。若貸款價值比超過 80%，可能會取得額外擔保品。在發放貸款資金前，會進行現場檢查以確認預設的建設進度。這些貸款通常有六至十二個月的償還期限，可能具有固定或變動利率特點。個人的永久融資選項包括具有三至五年期貸款到期特點的固定及變動利率貸款，以及一、三及五年期調整利率抵押貸款。本銀行透過保守的貸款審核程序，如貸款價值比在發放時為 80% 或更低、在適當情況下取得額外擔保品，以及密切監控建設項目以控制貸款資金的發放，來降低這些貸款的風險。

•商業貸款。本銀行為商業用途發放有擔保及無擔保貸款。商業貸款通常以不動產、應收帳款、存貨、設備及其他商業資產為擔保。償還通常取決於商業的運作成功，並可能受到當地經濟或不動產市場惡化條件的影響。因此，在貸款批准過程中，會仔細分析商業借款人的財務狀況及現金流，並持續監控以取得商業財務報表、個人財務報表及所得稅報表。此持續分析的頻率取決於貸款及擔保品的規模與複雜性。本銀行的總體政策亦為取得商業貸款借款人的主要負責人個人擔保。
•消費者貸款。為客戶提供多種消費者貸款，包括住宅 equity 貸款、船舶貸款及其他有擔保及無擔保信用線及期貨貸款。某些消費者貸款由第三方代表本公司發放。在發放貸款前，會對申請人的信用worthiness進行仔細分析，並持續監控現有貸款以盡可能降低損失風險，並及早識別問題貸款。本公司於 2023 年 6 月停止發行新的船舶貸款，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，僅服務現有貸款組合。
•信用卡貸款。本銀行為商業及消費者客戶提供無擔保信用卡貸款。信用風險因素包括借款人持續的財務穩定性，這可能因失業、離婚、疾病或個人破產等因素而受到不利影響。本公司於 2024 年 4 月停止發行新的信用卡（除特定現有信用卡客戶外），截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，僅服務現有貸款組合。

headings: 與總體經濟、財務市場、利率及流動性相關的風險
本公司營運地區集中，使我們易受當地經濟狀況下滑的影響。
利率變動可能對我們的營業收入與財務狀況產生不利影響。
通貨膨脹可能對我們的業務及客戶產生不利影響。
流動性不足可能影響我們資金營運的能力，並危及我們的財務狀況、成長與前景。
不利的總體經濟、市場及政治環境可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們的投資證券投資組合面臨信用風險、市場風險及流動性風險。
本公司針對信用損失之撥備可能無法充分覆蓋實際信用損失；針對信用損失之撥備增加可能不利於本公司財務狀況及營運成果。
本公司可能無法充分衡量並控制信用風險，此情形可能導致未預期之損失。
本公司之商業不動產貸款業務使其面臨較高之貸款風險及相關貸款損失。
銀行監管機構對商業不動產貸款業務設置限制，可能限制本公司之成長，並對本公司獲利產生不利影響。
本公司之住宅抵押貸款集中度使其面臨較高之貸款風險。
非 Performing 資產增加將對獲利產生不利影響。
評估可能無法準確反映本公司擔保品之價值。
本公司未來的成功將取決於我們在高度競爭的金融服務業中有效競爭的能力。
關鍵人員的流失可能幹擾本公司業務。
併購可能幹擾本公司業務。
本公司的資金來源可能證明不足以取代存款並支持未來的成長。
房貸銀行業務的收入波動性高，本公司可能針對房貸銀行業務產生虧損，這可能會對本公司的獲利產生負面影響。
本公司在處理違約房貸貸款的法拍程序上若有所延宕，可能會增加本公司的成本，並使本公司面臨更高的虧損風險。
聯邦政府對大麻相關法律的嚴格執行，可能會導致本公司無法繼續為大麻相關企業提供銀行服務，並使本公司面臨聯邦政府的法律訴訟。
本公司風險管理架構可能無法有效降低對本公司之風險及/或損失。
與財務報表相關之風險
本公司可能因投資證券發生減損費用，此可能對本公司營運成果、流動性、財務狀況或成長前景造成不利影響。
對商譽、其他無形資產或遞延所得稅資產之減損，可能導致需對營收計提費用，此將對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
會計準則之變更或對新舊準則之解釋方式改變，可能影響本公司財務狀況及營運成果之報導方式。
現行預期信用減損（"CECL"）會計準則可能導致本公司需提高信用減損準備金，並可能對本公司財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
本公司會計估計及風險管理程序依賴分析及預測模型。
本公司先前已識別出內部控制之重大缺陷。
我們依賴客戶與交易對手所提供之資訊之準確性與完整性，若我們依賴不正確資訊，本公司財務狀況可能受到不利影響。
營運風險，包括系統故障、人為錯誤及第三方依賴，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
與網路安全及科技相關之風險
本公司資訊系統可能遭遇中斷或安全漏洞。
安全漏洞及其他中斷事件可能影響本公司資訊，使本公司面臨法律責任，此將對本公司業務與聲譽造成損害。
未能遵守隱私權及資訊安全法規可能使本公司面臨法律責任。
本公司對第三方供應商之依賴可能使本公司面臨額外之網路風險與法律責任。
本公司將部分資料處理業務委外給特定第三方供應商，此可能使本公司面臨額外風險。
我們有風險因詐欺而導致損失增加。
未能跟上金融服務業的技術變革，可能對我們的競爭地位或獲利能力造成重大不利影響。
與我們產業相關的監管風險
我們營運於高度受規範的環境中，這可能會限制我們的成長與獲利能力。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及風險，包括投資價值可能大幅下跌，以及股息或其他分紅可能減少或取消。投資人應在決定投資本公司股票前，仔細考慮下列風險因素。下列風險因素可能導致本公司未來獲利較低，或財務狀況不如預期，這可能會對投資本公司之價值與回報產生不利影響。下列所述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為本公司所知或本公司認為不重要，這些風險與不確定性可能導致獲利較低，或對本公司財務狀況產生不利影響。投資人亦應考慮本年度10-K申報表，以及被引用至本10-K申報表之文件，因這些資訊可能隨本公司未來向證券交易委員會（SEC）提交之申報文件而更新。

本公司之銀行業務主要集中於馬裏蘭州東部與南部、德拉瓦州以及維吉尼亞州北部。本公司之成功在一定程度上取決於這些地區之經濟狀況。華盛頓特區都會區特徵為有大量企業為聯邦政府承包商或分包商，或這些企業之收入有相當大一部分取決於這些政府承包商。此外，聯邦政府員工在華盛頓特區都會區人口中佔有相當比例。若因裁員、買斷工資、停薪留職或政府員工或承包商遭解僱，以及政府契約取消或其他因政府支出減少、預算停擺或財政預算變動所導致之影響，可能對本公司市場中其他企業及華盛頓特區都會區整體經濟產生不利影響。若本公司市場之經濟狀況出現不利變化，可能限制貸款與存款之成長，影響本公司收取貸款應收款之能力，增加問題貸款與核銷金額，並對本公司營運與財務狀況產生其他負面影響。房地產價值下跌可能導致本公司部分住宅與商業房地產貸款之擔保不足，這將使本公司在貸款違約後，若透過緊急出售擔保房地產以償還貸款，可能面臨較高之損失風險。

本公司之淨利潤在很大程度上取決於淨利息收入，即貸款、投資及其他利息收入資產所產生之利息收入，與存款及借款等利息負債所支付之利息之差額。淨利息收入會因市場利率變動而受到影響，因不同類型之資產與負債可能對市場利率變動反應不同，且反應時間亦不同。當利息負債之到期日或重新定價日比利息收入資產之到期日或重新定價日更早時，市場利率上升可能導致淨利息收入減少。同樣地，當利息收入資產之到期日或重新定價日比利息負債之到期日或重新定價日更早時，利率下降可能導致淨利息收入減少。

市場利率變動受許多因素影響，而這些因素均超出本公司控制範圍，包括通貨膨脹、失業率、貨幣供給、美國政府之財政政策、國內與國際事件，以及美國及其他金融市場之事件。本公司試圖透過調整不同類型之利息收入資產與利息負債之利率、到期日、重新定價日與餘額，來管理市場利率變動之風險，但利率風險管理技術並非完全準確。因此，利率快速上升或下降可能對本公司營運結果產生不利影響。不同市場中各種產品與服務之市場利率變動，也可能因地區與時間不同，而有顯著差異，這取決於競爭與當地或區域性經濟因素。
有關利率變動對淨利息收入之影響之進一步討論，請參閱本報告之第7A項。任何利率敏感度模擬模型之結果均依賴於有關客戶行為、利率變動與現金流之假設，而這些假設可能證明不正確。

通貨膨脹通常會提高本公司業務運作中所使用之商品與服務之成本，以及勞動成本。本公司可能發現需要給予員工較高於正常水平之加薪，並以較高工資聘用新員工。此外，本公司客戶亦受高通貨膨脹影響，並面臨其家庭與企業所使用之商品與服務成本上升，這可能會影響其償還本公司貸款之能力。歷史上，美國聯邦準備理事會（Federal Reserve）曾提高聯邦基金目標利率，以對抗高通貨膨脹。市場利率通常會因聯邦準備理事會之行動而上升。市場利率上升會提高借款成本，並壓抑貸款需求。當市場利率上升時，本公司之投資證券價值通常會下降，不過此影響對浮動利率工具可能較不顯著。較高的利率會提高替代性投資與儲蓄產品（如美國國庫券與貨幣市場基金）之吸引力，這可能使吸引與保留存款變得困難。持續較高的利率可能削弱經濟活動。美國與本公司市場之經濟狀況惡化，可能會導致貸款違約率進一步上升與非表現貸款資產增加、貸款擔保價值下降，以及對本公司產品與服務之需求減少，所有這些情況，將進一步對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生不利影響。
